title: The folder read in full every night
outcome: A hand-written load appended the whole landing folder each night, and every order was counted once more each day.

content.bookmark: COPY INTO and Auto Loader remember which files they have loaded. A plain read of a folder doesn't, so appending it again loads everything again.

check.prompt: COPY INTO runs again over a folder that still holds yesterday's files. What happens to those files?
options: The command fails, because a file it has seen before must be removed from the folder first
They are skipped: files already loaded aren't loaded again
check.why: COPY INTO is retriable and idempotent: files it has already loaded are skipped on later runs.

check.prompt: What does Databricks recommend to SQL users as the alternative to COPY INTO for loading files incrementally?
options: CREATE STREAMING TABLE, using Auto Loader
A nightly INSERT OVERWRITE of the whole folder
spark.read with a filter on the file date
check.why: The ingestion pages name CREATE STREAMING TABLE (with Auto Loader) as the recommended alternative to COPY INTO.

check.prompt: How does Auto Loader know which files it has already processed?
options: It renames each processed file in the source folder, adding a suffix it checks on the next run
It keeps file metadata in RocksDB in the checkpoint location
It reads the target table's history and compares file names with the last commit
check.why: Discovered files are tracked in RocksDB in the checkpoint location, which gives exactly-once processing and lets a failed stream resume.

check.prompt: Which MERGE appends only the records a table doesn't already hold?
options: MERGE ... WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET *
MERGE ... ON t.id = s.id WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *
MERGE ... WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE, removing rows the batch lacks
check.why: An insert-only merge on a unique key appends only new records: the documented way to avoid duplicates when a batch is replayed.

caseStudy.setting: A ticketing company (fictional) receives box-office sales as CSV files, a few new files every night, in an ADLS container registered as an external location. To get started quickly, an engineer wrote a notebook that reads the whole folder with spark.read.csv and appends the result to a bronze table. It runs nightly as a job.

events.what: Everything looks right. Bronze row counts rise every night, which everyone expects.
Finance notices ticket revenue in the gold report is far above the box-office system's own figures, and the gap grows each day.
An engineer finds that bronze holds the first night's files twenty times over. Each run read every file in the folder, not just the new ones.

pipeline: Box-office CSV files · ADLS container, files never removed
Silver and gold · built from bronze by later tasks
tasks: How should the load work, and how do you repair the data?

debrief.title: Why the counts grew
text: spark.read.csv on a folder reads every file in it. Nothing records what an earlier run loaded, so each nightly append added all the old files again plus the new ones.
On night n, the first night's files were in bronze n times. The duplicates flowed into silver and gold.

debrief.title: Loading only new files
text: COPY INTO skips files it has already loaded, so it can run every night over the same folder. It is retriable: a failed run can simply run again.
Auto Loader does the same as a stream, tracking files in its checkpoint, and scales to far more files. Run with availableNow, it processes what has arrived and stops, which suits a nightly job.
For SQL users, Databricks recommends a streaming table with Auto Loader over COPY INTO. Databricks also recommends starting with the most managed ingestion option that fits.

debrief.title: Repairing the data
text: Rebuild bronze once with the new load, then rebuild silver and gold from it. Bronze is the base for reprocessing, which is exactly what this needs.
Where a replay could still happen, an insert-only MERGE on a unique key (such as a ticket id) keeps duplicates out of later layers.

takeaway: Reading a folder isn't incremental; COPY INTO and Auto Loader are.
Choose the most managed ingestion option that fits.
A replay-safe write (insert-only MERGE on a key) is a second line of defence.
content.honesty: If you haven't built a file ingestion pipeline, say so, and explain the difference between reading a folder and tracking files. If you have cleaned up duplicated data, describe how you found it.

tasks: What check would have caught this in week 1?
What would you add to acceptance criteria for a data load?

debrief.title: An early check
text: Reconcile a total with the source system: ticket revenue in the report against the box-office figure, every day.

debrief.title: Acceptance criteria
text: Running the load twice on the same files changes nothing.
Daily totals match the source system within an agreed tolerance.

sayIt.question: How do you know the numbers in a data product are right?
points: Reconcile key totals against the source system regularly.
Make reruns safe: running a load twice must not double data.
Track rows in and rows out at each layer.
Give a named owner to each reconciliation.
Tell users how fresh and how checked the data is.

tasks: How do you plan the repair?

debrief.title: Finance
text: Ticket revenue in the report has been overstated since launch because some sales were loaded many times. Corrected figures by a named date; the box-office system's own numbers are right.

debrief.title: The repair
text: Rebuild bronze with an incremental load, rebuild silver and gold, then reconcile against the source before announcing the fix.

sayIt.question: A report has shown wrong numbers for three weeks. How do you handle it?
points: Tell the affected users quickly, with what is wrong and what isn't.
Give a date for corrected figures.
Fix the cause, then the data, then reconcile.
Check whether any decisions used the wrong figures.
Add a reconciliation so it is caught early next time.

tasks: How do you sequence the fix?
What standard should come out of it?

debrief.title: Sequence
text: Stop the nightly job, switch to COPY INTO or Auto Loader, rebuild bronze, rebuild silver and gold, reconcile, then restart the schedule.

debrief.title: Standard
text: Every file load is incremental and safe to rerun; a reconciliation against the source is part of done.

sayIt.question: How would you plan rebuilding a data pipeline's tables without breaking reports?
points: Fix the load first, so the rebuild isn't immediately undone.
Rebuild layers in order: bronze, then silver, then gold.
Reconcile before switching users over.
Tell users when figures will change.
Keep a way back until the new figures are confirmed.

tasks: What would you replace the notebook with?

debrief.title: Replacement
text: COPY INTO sales_raw FROM the folder with FILEFORMAT = CSV, or Auto Loader with trigger(availableNow=True) and its own checkpoint, or a streaming table defined in SQL.
Add _metadata.file_name to bronze so every row says which file it came from.

debrief.title: Rebuilding
text: Recreate bronze from the files with the new load, then rerun silver and gold; check row counts per file against the source.

sayIt.question: Compare COPY INTO and Auto Loader for loading files into Delta tables.
points: Both load only new files: COPY INTO skips files it already loaded; Auto Loader tracks them in its checkpoint.
COPY INTO is a SQL command, retriable and idempotent.
Auto Loader is a Structured Streaming source (cloudFiles) that scales to billions of files.
Auto Loader adds schema inference, evolution and the rescued data column.
Databricks recommends streaming tables with Auto Loader for SQL users.
